key_insight: A single RL-trained model is treated as a local probe of a larger reasoning manifold, so better students come from constructing and compressing a complementary union of teachers rather than choosing one best teacher.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical recipe for boosting small-model reasoning quality while keeping single-model inference, which is useful for deployable math, code, and instruction-following systems.
method: RGRPO expands coverage by training multiple teachers from one initialization and steering later rounds toward uncovered examples.
TU-OPD compresses the teacher union into a student using reliability-gated, on-policy distillation from the student’s own response prefixes.
Consensus-Residual Decomposition preserves a winner teacher’s extra token preferences so specialist behaviors are not averaged away.
evidence_signal: On math reasoning, code generation, and instruction following, the Qwen3-1.7B student beat the strongest individual teacher with reported relative gains of 2.0%, 8.3%, and 6.9%.
watch_item: The approach adds training complexity and depends on reliable teacher selection/quality scoring, which may be sensitive to implementation details and domain coverage.
paper_title: Beyond the Best Teacher: Expanding and Compressing the Reasoning Solution Manifold
